data.long_meaning: The name Carissae is derived from the Greek word καρδιάζω (kardiazō), meaning 'to love' or 'to cherish'. In the Bible, this name is given to a few characters who were deeply loved, such as Sarah, the wife of Abraham, and Mary, the mother of Jesus. The name Carissae carries the meaning “Beloved” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Carissae usually hope their child will grow to embody beloved and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: קריסאי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קריסאי (K'rYsAy) היא שם נשי שמקורו ביוונית. השם יפה, נשגב, ומערכה. השם קרוי על שם היופי החיצוני והפנימי של האדם. במסורת היהודית, השם קריסאי מופיע כשם של יופי ושל יפה-יופי. השם קריסאי גם מופיע בספרות הקדומה של יוון, שם הוא מסמל יופי ושגביות. במסורת הנוצרית, השם קריסאי נחשב לשם נשי של יופי ושל יפה-יופי גם כן.

in_greek.name: Καρίσαι
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Καρίσαι (Karisai) είναι ένα γυναικείο όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη για την αγάπη. Τον 4ο αιώνα μ.Χ., το όνομα Καρίσαι ήταν κοινό στα Βυζαντινά βραβεία. Στη χριστιανική παράδοση, ο Καρίσαι είναι ένα όνομα που δείχνει την αγάπη και την πίστη. Το όνομα Καρίσαι σχετίζεται με το όνομα της Αγίας Μαρίας, που είναι μια από τις πρώτες χριστιανές.

in_latin.name: Carissae
in_latin.long_meaning: Carissae, nomen femininum, a lingua Graeca originem ducit. In ecclesiastica traditione, Carissae significat amorem et fidem. Carissae nominis origo a Carissimo, titulo sanctae Mariae, derivatur.

historical_references.reference: Carissae was a Greek city located in the region of Phocis. It was an important religious site for the ancient Greeks, dedicated to the goddesses Demeter and Persephone. During the Hellenistic period, Carissae was part of the Kingdom of Macedon. In 168 BC, it was sacked by the Roman consul Lucius Mummius Achaicus, who was campaigning against the Achaean League. After the Roman conquest, Carissae became a Roman colonia, with a Latin colony established there.
historical_references.context: Roman conquest of the Achaean League

historical_references.reference: In the early Christian period, Carissae was known as a place of pilgrimage for Christians. According to tradition, the apostles Philip and James the Less visited the city in the 1st century AD, and a church was built there in their honor. The city was also believed to be the site of a miraculous well, which was said to have healing properties. Carissae became an important center of Christian pilgrimage during the Byzantine period.
